scalars.scalar_value: All staff positions, regardless of remote work eligibility, require an initial 30-calendar-day on-campus work period. Based on an evaluation by the Area Leadership Group (supervisor, area leader and area Cabinet member) and HR, this position is classified as Category A as defined in the College’s Remote Work Policy, with no ad-hoc remote work flexibility. Your position is essential to on-campus operations and requires you to work exclusively on campus. Additionally, remote work is subject to the College’s remote work policy. The College reserves the right to revoke or modify a remote work arrangement for any staff, at any time and for any reason, as articulated in the College’s remote work policy.
This position reports to the Student Affairs Administrator/Special Projects Lead
This is a non-exempt, part-time, temporary, up to 20 hours per week, non-benefits eligible position. The anticipated duration of this position is July 1, 2026 to May 29, 2027

Assist the Student Affairs Administrator/Special Projects Lead in coordinating projects across the division.
Support with student reimbursements and funding.
Create and distribute promotional materials, including flyers, presentations, newsletters, social media content, and other communication materials.
Assist with maintaining departmental communications, websites, and outreach efforts.
Support marketing and recruitment efforts for Student Affairs programs and initiatives.
Assist with data collection, assessment, and reporting efforts related to Student Affairs programs and services.
Maintain accurate records, documentation, and project materials.
Complete weekly updates and progress reports as directed by the supervisor.
Support divisional priorities and strategic initiatives as assigned.
Participate in cross-functional projects that support the goals of the Dean of Students Office and Division of Student Affairs.
Prepare transition documents and resource materials to support continuity of operations.
Provide support for departmental operations as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Excellent interpersonal, writing, and verbal communication skills.
Ability to work effectively with HMC students.
Ability to work independently and exercise good judgment in decision-making.
Ability to prioritize multiple duties/tasks and meet deadlines.
Ability to think strategically, plan effectively, and manage projects/events.
Personal integrity and demonstrated commitment to high standards and attention to detail.
Ability to thrive in a collaborative team environment and interact successfully with individuals with varying abilities, backgrounds, interests, and beliefs.
Ability to work weekends depending on programmatic needs.
Adept at using software such as Microsoft Office Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Adobe Acrobat.

pay.source_text: The anticipated starting salary is $17.50/hour. Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
